subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
skillName: Patterns of Motion Predict Future Motion
intro: Many objects move in regular, repeating patterns. A swing goes back and forth the same way each time, a ball on a curved track rolls the same path, and the hands of a clock move in a steady pattern. When we observe and measure a pattern of motion, we can use it to predict what the object will do next. For example, if a swing takes the same time for each back-and-forth, we can predict when it will return. Patterns make motion predictable.

items.prompt: A swing takes the same amount of time to go back and forth each time. How can this pattern be used to predict its motion?

steps: The swing repeats the same back-and-forth motion in the same time.
Because the pattern repeats, the next swing will take the same time.
So you can predict when the swing will return to where it started.
solution.answer: Because the swing repeats the same timing, you can predict it will return at the same, regular time.

items.prompt: A ball rolls down the same curved track three times and follows the same path each time. What can you predict about the fourth roll?

steps: The ball followed the same path on each of the first three rolls.
This is a repeating pattern of motion.
So you can predict the fourth roll will follow the same path.
solution.answer: You can predict the fourth roll will follow the same path as the earlier rolls.

items.prompt: Why does observing a pattern of motion let us predict future motion?

steps: A pattern means the motion repeats in a regular way.
If it keeps repeating the same way, the next motion will match the pattern.
So the pattern gives us a reliable way to predict what happens next.
solution.answer: Because a repeating pattern keeps happening the same way, so we can expect the next motion to match it.

items.prompt: Name one object that moves in a repeating pattern.

steps: Repeating patterns of motion happen in many objects.
A swing (or a clock's hands, or a bouncing ball) moves in a repeating pattern.
solution.answer: A swing (also a clock's hands or a pendulum).

items.prompt: A student measures that a pendulum swings 10 times in 20 seconds. Predict how many times it will swing in 40 seconds, and explain.

steps: The pendulum swings at a steady, repeating rate.
In 20 seconds it swings 10 times, so in twice the time it should swing twice as many.
So in 40 seconds it should swing about 20 times.
solution.answer: About 20 times, because the steady pattern means twice the time gives about twice the swings.

items.prompt: A toy train goes around a loop track in 15 seconds each time. A student wants to know where it will be in 30 seconds. How does the pattern help?

steps: The train takes the same time, 15 seconds, for each full loop.
In 30 seconds it completes two full loops.
So it will be back at the same starting spot, which the repeating pattern lets you predict.
solution.answer: The train completes two loops in 30 seconds and returns to the start, which the repeating pattern predicts.
